Pipeline (unit probe on the new overload). undecoded=True for:
- /Foo, /Fl and /CCF
- Flate 'xxxxxxx', and zlib with byte 1 or byte 2 complemented
- [/Crypt /Foo] and [/Foo /Crypt]
- [null] and [9 0 R] where object 9 is missing
- 5, << >> and (FlateDecode)
- [/FlateDecode /Foo], whose data is the Flate output
- [/Foo /DCTDecode]
- [/FlateDecode /DCTDecode] whose Flate fails
- a failing inner Flate under [/FlateDecode /FlateDecode]
undecoded=False for:
- image filters, and [/DCTDecode /Foo]
- /Crypt and [/Crypt], [] and null
- a missing reference as the /Filter entry
- a predictor that fails, or one of unknown type
- garbage data under LZW, ASCIIHex, ASCII85 or RunLength
- empty data
- Flate of a header only (it runs out)
- a checksum mismatch
- a 65th filter (leftEncoded instead)
- /DecodeParms arrays shorter or longer than /Filter
leftEncoded and undecoded are never both true. undecoded and cutByGuard can both be true, for [/FlateDecode /Foo] past MaxDecodedStreamLength; the reader then gives the file's fault, as a whole read does.

Other callers are unchanged. PdfStream.Decode, in memory and in a document, gives byte-identical output and reports on head and d3ef236 for /Foo, failing Flate, byte-0-damaged Flate, DCT and [/FlateDecode /Foo]. So does an object stream with failing Flate. Main differs only in #241's '1 object' wording. By construction, DecodeChain's return values are untouched.

/Prev hand-on with undecodable data (#208): a /Prev that is a reference, negative, past the file, the stream's own offset (chain-cycle plus Error chain-loop) or absent. Each is reported once and in order: the filter report, then section-unreadable with the right tail, then the /Prev's own report. The rebuild serves 'only in the stream' and 'new seven'.
Refusal under B19-2: no /Index with /Size 9 or /Size 2,000,000,000 refuses [0, /Size) and rebuilds at opening without cost. A stream of no /Type at /Prev is Malformed and its objects are rebuilt.

/XRefStm naming such a stream in place gives [filter.failed, xref.section-unreadable]. Named 3 bytes off, it gives [filter.failed, xref.offset-adjusted, xref.section-unreadable 'found at'], plus Warning section-shifted, and serves 'new three' through the rebuild. d3ef236 served null there.

Guards:
- MaxDecodedStreamLength 8 on [/FlateDecode /Foo] gives limit.decoded-stream, filter.unsupported, then section-unreadable as the file's fault, the whole read's verdict.
- Under ThrowOnLimit it throws PdfLimitExceededException.
- MaxFilterChainLength 1 gives the guard's limit.filter-chain and xref.checked-in-part.
- MaxStreamLength 8 under /Foo gives the file's fault.
- /W cut, and an /Index count cut, give the file's fault under the guard as read whole, with the filter report once.

An extra catalog mutant, dropping '|| declared <= most.Rows' in FaultBesideCut, is killed by 12 GuardCutValueTests failures.

No allocation is added on a valid file's path: the read loop takes one more out bool, and relocation, the check and FaultBesideCut are paths only damaged files take. The search copies the decoding-report table once per candidate, at most MaxRelocationCandidates (32) copies over a document.

Filter reports appear exactly once, in a stable order, in every probe: found in place, found moved, as the /Prev, the /XRefStm, startxref, under a guard and read whole. Decoding after opening re-reports a dropped candidate's decoding report once.
